title: Crypto marketing agency alternative for early-stage projects
author: Cryptool
excerpt_html: An agency retainer or a first marketing hire is the usual answer to invisibility. Both are expensive, slow to start, and still leave gaps.
content_html:
Every crypto project reaches the same point: the product is real, nobody knows about it, and the two conventional answers are hiring an agency or hiring a first marketer. Both are real options and sometimes the right one. Both are also expensive, take one to three months to produce anything, and leave the day to day continuous work uncovered. GTM is a go-to-market app that runs that continuous work, and it comes with your Cryptool account.

What an agency genuinely gives you

Judgement, relationships and accountability, and those are not small things. A good crypto agency knows which publications matter, has contacts at them, has watched dozens of launches, and will tell you when your positioning is wrong. That is expertise you cannot generate, and if you are preparing a token launch with real capital behind it, hire one. Nothing below is an argument against that.

What it does not give you

Retainers buy a defined scope, and the always-on work usually sits outside it. Posting consistently between campaigns, keeping search presence alive, noticing a mention on the day it happens rather than in the monthly report: these are continuous obligations and retainers are billed in months. There is also a ramp problem, since an agency needs weeks to learn your project before output starts, and a dependency problem, since the knowledge leaves when the contract ends.

A first marketing hire fixes the dependency but is a large fixed cost, takes time to recruit and longer to become productive, and is one person who cannot simultaneously write content, run SEO, manage paid search, monitor mentions and do outreach. Those are four or five jobs, and expecting one hire to do them all is the most common way early-stage marketing fails.

What GTM covers

Content, written and published on-brand across your connected channels, continuously rather than in campaign bursts.

Search, both organic and paid. SEO and search engine advertising run as part of the same system.

Mention tracking, so you know where and when the project is being discussed instead of finding out in a report.

Support for outreach, sales and partnership or M&A motions, so visibility connects to a commercial conversation.

No ramp and no notice period. You set up the brand and connect channels, and it runs from there.

The honest way to think about it

This is not really agency versus tool, because they do different things. A tool cannot call a journalist, judge whether your narrative is credible to a specific investor, or take responsibility for a launch. An agency cannot be present every day for what a retainer costs. The realistic sequence for most projects is to run the continuous work through GTM, and bring in an agency for the moments that need human judgement and relationships, a launch, a listing, a crisis. What you should not do is pay agency rates for output a system can produce, or expect one junior hire to cover five disciplines.

Common questions

Can GTM replace an agency entirely?

For the continuous work, largely. For relationships, press, judgement calls on narrative and accountability for a launch, no, and we would rather say that than oversell it.

How quickly does it start producing?

You set up your brand and connect channels, and it works from that setup, with no recruitment or onboarding period.

What does it cost?

It comes with your Cryptool account rather than as a separate subscription.

Do I still need someone in-house?

Someone should own the positioning and make the judgement calls, but that is a few hours of decisions rather than a full-time execution role. The failure mode GTM addresses is the gap between decisions and daily output.
